newsitem.title: USA: All 11 Atlanta school districts approve tax hike.
newsitem.headline: All 11 Atlanta school districts approve tax hike.

text.p: Voters in all 11 Atlanta-area school districts approved one-cent sales tax increases that will raise a combined $2.4 billion for construction and debt retirement over five years, school officials said Wednesday.
The money will be used to build more than 50 new schools, eliminate 1,000 temporary trailer classrooms and retire at least $463 million of oustanding bonds issued by the 11 districts.
The sales tax hikes were approved in referendums Tuesday in eight counties -- Clayton, Coweta, DeKalb, Douglas, Forsyth, Fulton, Gwinnet and Paulding.
In addition to the eight county school districts, three city school districts in those counties -- Atlanta, Buford and Decatur -- will receive pro-rated shares of the revenue.
Votes within the city districts were not counted separately in the countywide elections, a spokeswoman with the Atlanta school district said.
The proposals passed by margins of nearly 2-1 in all but Coweta County, where it squeaked by with 52 percent of the votes, and Paulding County, where it passed with 57 percent.
Voter turnout was generally below 20 percent, school officials said.
